name: Quartermaster
description: A per-chat RPG character sheet and inventory manager for Roleplay mode: equip slots arranged around your persona's portrait, a full inventory with saved outfits, AI-generated item and outfit art, and a tracker agent that keeps everything in sync with the story on its own.
author: ThatOneCan
defaultPromptTemplate:
Track changes to the persona's equipped items and inventory after the latest message in this roleplay. Current inventory is in <agent_runtime_context>, with each item and outfit shown behind a bracketed tag ([1], [2]... for items; [A], [B]... for outfits) -- always refer to an EXISTING item or outfit by that tag, never by retyping its name.

Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no prose, no markdown:
{
  "reasoning": "brief explanation",
  "addItem": [
    { "name": "string", "description": "string (optional)", "quantity": integer >= 1, "location": "bag" | "equipped:<slot>" | "stored:<free text>" }
  ],
  "updateItem": [
    { "target": <item tag number>, "description": "string (optional, OMIT if unchanged)", "quantity": integer >= 0 (optional, OMIT if unchanged), "location": "..." (optional, OMIT if unchanged) }
  ],
  "removeItem": [ <item tag number>, ... ],
  "equipOutfit": <outfit tag letter, or null>
}

Always include all four keys, even when nothing applies -- "addItem": [], "updateItem": [], "removeItem": [], "equipOutfit": null is a completely valid response when nothing changed this turn.

Valid slots (use these exact ids only): head, neck, eyes, ears, armor_torso, armor_legs, clothing_torso, clothing_legs, underwear_top, underwear_bottom, back, hands, weapon_left_hand, weapon_right_hand, feet, belt.

EXAMPLE -- given this context:
Items:
[1] Rusty Dagger -- a chipped old blade (qty 1, bag)
[2] Traveler's Cloak -- a worn grey cloak (qty 1, equipped:back)
Outfits:
[A] Merchant Disguise

...and narration "She tucked the dagger away and pulled a fresh red scarf from her pack, wrapping it around her neck.", the correct response is:
{
  "reasoning": "The dagger is already in the bag, unchanged, so it needs no entry at all. A new scarf appears and is worn around the neck.",
  "addItem": [{ "name": "Red Scarf", "description": "a fresh red scarf", "quantity": 1, "location": "equipped:neck" }],
  "updateItem": [],
  "removeItem": [],
  "equipOutfit": null
}

RULES:
1. Only include an item under "updateItem" or "removeItem" if something about it actually changed or it's genuinely gone. An item just mentioned in passing, unchanged, needs NO entry at all -- omitting it does nothing to it.
2. Target an EXISTING item or outfit only by its bracketed tag from <agent_runtime_context> -- never by retyping its name.
3. "addItem" is for something the persona didn't have before. If it's the same thing as something already listed (matching name, just picked back up or referenced again), use "updateItem" on its existing tag instead -- never create a second entry for the same item. Visually or materially different items still need clearly different names ("Blue Hat" and "Red Hat" are different items, not both "Hat").
4. On "updateItem", only include a field you are actually changing. Leave out "description"/"quantity"/"location" entirely when they are not changing -- do not repeat the current value, and never send a blank placeholder for a field you don't mean to change. Each field you DO include fully replaces that one field; every field you leave out stays exactly as it was.
5. Each equip slot holds ONE item -- moving something new into an occupied slot automatically unequips whatever was there. You don't need to manage this yourself.
6. Use "equipOutfit" (the outfit's tag letter) when the persona puts on a saved outfit BY NAME/description matching one of the outfits listed. Equipped slots apply from the outfit automatically -- don't also list its items under "updateItem". Leave "equipOutfit" null otherwise, and equip/unequip individual items via "updateItem"'s own "location" field instead.
7. Keep an item's name STABLE across turns unless the prose renames it.
8. "quantity" is a non-negative integer, and always the ABSOLUTE current amount -- never a +1/-1 delta. 0 means "used up but still tracked" -- keep it at 0 rather than using "removeItem", unless it's genuinely gone (thrown away, given away, destroyed).
9. "location" is "bag" (carried, unequipped), "equipped:<slot>" (worn or wielded -- one of the slots listed above), or "stored:<name>" (left somewhere specific, e.g. "stored:home").
10. Touch at most about 20 items in one response. If a scene genuinely changes more than that, cover only the narratively significant ones.
